newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London firm, await earnings news.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London firm, await earnings news.

text.p: U.S. shares were mostly firmer on Monday, following Wall Street's 45-point advance last Friday but trading volumes remained light as European investors continued to fret about the sustainability of the Dow's recent rally.
With few important economic statistics due out this week, the market is expected to concentrate on corporate earnings and trading statements, dealers said.
"The tone is firmer this morning but people are still worried about the Dow taking another nose-dive," one market maker said.
"If we get any earnings shocks the Dow could give up last week's gains."

Since April 11, when the Dow closed at a 1997 low of 6,391.6, U.S. blue chips have risen a net 312 points but the top 30 share index is still 382 points below its all-time closing high of 7,085.16, set on March 11.

AT&T was down $3/8 to $33-3/8 ahead of the release of its first quarter figures, due later today. News last week of the British Telecommunications link-up with Spain's Telefonica de Espana weighed on the share price, dealers said.
"The BT deal really dashed AT&T's global expansion plans, especially in Latin America," one dealer said."
WMX Technologies Inc was up $1/4 to $31-1/8 ahead of its latest quarterly numbers.

The shares benefited from renewed speculation about the timing of the appointment of a new chief executive after the company said on Friday that the chairman and acting CEO Dean Buntrock planned to step aside when a new skipper came aboard.
Elsewhere, Chrysler Corp was down $1/4 to $30-1/8 over concerns about the 10-day old strike at one of its engine plants that has so far cost the auto maker up to $20 million a day in lost profits.
"The talk now is that if this strike goes on much longer, Chrysler will report a loss in the second quarter," one dealer said.
Citicorp was up $3/8 to $103-5/8 after press reports said the company was shifting leadership of its consumer-bank unit and planned to streamline management of worldwide operations.
The June S&P 500 futures contract was down 0.45 to 769.80 while the June T-bond rose 2/32 to 108-2/32 by 1055 GMT.
